patients.label: 28-year-old pregnant woman at 35 weeks of gestation with chronic dysphonia, fever and cough diagnosed with laryngeal tuberculosis after an initial laryngeal cancer report

identity_evidence.quote: We present the case of a 28-year-old pregnant woman with 35 weeks of gestation, from Loreto, Peru.

attribution_limitations: An outside laryngoscopy report concluded laryngeal cancer without a biopsy and the authors then list laryngeal cancer and laryngeal tuberculosis as differential diagnoses; the source never excludes cancer histologically.

The source never states a pulmonary tuberculosis diagnosis for the patient: it reports a highly suspected lung infection as the starting point and radiographic alterations compatible with pulmonary tuberculosis, with a hedged bronchogenic route. Pulmonary tuberculosis is therefore provisional and review_only.
The respiratory frequency is printed as 14 vpm and described as increased, alongside tachypnea on examination.
The sputum bacilloscopy grade is printed as (+/+++) without further explanation.
The pregnancy outcome, delivery and fetal or newborn status are not reported.
The antituberculous regimen total duration and completion are not stated for the patient; the six-month minimum appears only as a general discussion statement.

claims.text: A 28-year-old woman at 35 weeks of gestation from Loreto, Peru had four months of progressive dysphonia, 5 kg weight loss, dry cough and dysphagia, then odynophagia, fever, night sweats and productive cough one month before admission. She was admitted to the emergency room with respiratory distress and hemoptysis, bringing a laryngoscopy report that concluded laryngeal cancer, although no biopsy had been performed.

claims.text: Examination showed bad general condition, tachypnea, dysphonia, decreased subcutaneous tissue, temperature 39 °C and increased heart and respiratory rates. Laryngeal cancer and laryngeal tuberculosis were proposed as differential diagnoses. A new laryngoscopy showed a mamelonated laryngeal tumoration with irregular vocal cords of limited mobility. Sputum bacilloscopy was positive and chest radiography showed bibasal nodular lesions and left apical opacities, raising high suspicion of laryngeal tuberculosis secondary to lung infection. Laryngeal biopsy was not possible.
